info.name: Reference Scheduler API
info.description:
Comprehensive Newman/Postman suite for Reference.Scheduler.Server.

Auth: OpenIddict password-grant (POST /connect/token, form-encoded).
Access token stored in {{accessToken}}, sent as Authorization: Bearer.
Preview slot base URL: {{baseUrl}} = https://sched-mt.preview.cyberdynedevelopment.dev/api/v1

Run:
  newman run Reference-Scheduler.postman_collection.json -e Reference-Scheduler.postman_environment.json

item.name: POST — Trigger limitation: Interval body ignored (cron-only DTO)

request.description: The Create DTO (CreateScheduleRequest) only has Name/PipelineName/CronExpression. intervalSeconds/schedulerType in the body are ignored, so an Interval/Once/Manual schedule cannot be created via POST. This is a real limitation documented in newman-matrix.md. Interval/Once/Manual are exercised via PUT instead.

exec: // ---- assertion helpers (copied from FDW-Reference-API gold-standard collection) ----
// assertScheduleInfoShape: validate a ScheduleInfo DTO from list/get responses.
// The Create DTO ignores intervalSeconds/schedulerType — only cron is honored.
pm.test('create accepts request (201) but cannot set Interval via POST', function () { pm.expect([201, 400]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

item.name: PUT — Trigger via PUT: Interval (200) [blocked: SCH-20 persist]

request.description: Interval/Once/Manual trigger types cannot be created via POST (cron-only DTO). PUT is the only path to exercise them. Note: schedulerType is currently NOT applied by the merge in UpdateScheduleEndpoint, and SCH-20 means changes do not persist — so this only validates the endpoint accepts the body.

exec: pm.test('PUT with interval body accepted (200)', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });
// schedulerType is not applied by the merge; SCH-20 prevents persistence. Documented in matrix.
pm.test('empty-body update succeeds (existing preserved) (200)', function () { pm.expect([200, 400]).to.include(pm.response.code); });
